reason:
Drove state=print at 1440x960 and harvested every visible text node under .b-print. One of the three claimed repetitions survives; two do not.

SURVIVES (leg 1, today's date twice in full ceremonial form). Verified co-occurring on the sheet: .b-unit reads "days away on Thursday 16 July 2026" (x550 y253, 11px, ink 0.72) and .b-origin reads "Today, Thursday 16 July 2026" (x772 y160, 11px, ink 0.72) — same string, same size, same ink density, same top third, ~240px apart across the column gutter. Both are print-only special cases in render-b.js: line 98 lengthens the unit on paper ("on a sheet it is the unit and the day the figure was true") and line 180 independently lengthens the origin on paper (medium==="print" ? longYear : medium). The renderer already states the governing rule at lines 121-125, where .b-todayLabel is deleted on print with the comment "Today is a screen fact. On paper it is already in the line above, and a second, differently grammared one dates the sheet twice." That exact rule was applied to one today-line and not to the other; the origin is also the only long-form date in its own column, where every row beneath it is short ("Sat 1 Aug", "Sat 3 Oct"). The origin's documented job — give the rail its own anchor for "now" so the instrument reads without the other column — is fully served by "Today, 16 July"; the year is carried by the dateline, by the wedding date and by the unit line. The fix therefore deletes a print branch rather than adding one, and costs the sheet nothing.

REFUTED (leg 2, the cancelled moment). Already handled, and the proposed fix is already in the code. behindBlock renders the behind-you summary sentence as `listed ? null : h("p.b-behindNote", {"data-when":"folded"})` — on paper o.print===true forces listed, so the prose that would name the cancelled item ("The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead.") never prints. The harvest confirms it: exactly one .b-behindNote on the sheet. The line that does print, "One of them did not happen.", is a different node with a different job — it partitions the "3 moments" total the head carries — and the code comment at that site ("Two closings, one shown") shows the dedupe was already reasoned and landed. Suppressing "the summary sentence" would remove nothing that is on the page.

REFUTED (leg 3, the gap sentence). The finding does not propose changing it, and the reason it gives for keeping it is factually wrong about the sheet: it claims the sentence "adds a boundary date the rail does not print". The rail prints it — .b-date "Sat 1 Aug" at x772 y311, on the first row.

Confirmed on leg 1 only, because it is verified on the uncorrectable surface, is a one-line deletion, and removes a redundancy the artifact's own stated rule already forbids. Legs 2 and 3 are not defects and must not be actioned.
